decision: frm PDM30:OUT7 -> SPL-PDM30-OUT7 (PDM30:OUT7 pigtails B5 + B11) — the 16 AWG load wire starts at the in-line M81824/1-3; the two 16 AWG pigtails 54_PT1/_PT2 land on PDM30 B5 and B11 (review A1 (receipt 2026-09-28_reviews-and-shape-rules.md; state 0h(1)): MoTeC PDM user manual p.48 — 20# to 16# on 20 A outputs, 16# = 15 A at 80 C, each pin carries about half the output; Superseal SSC-N contact 24-16 AWG (ProWire M800-KIT-N); in-line MiniSeal M81824/1-3 (ProWire Raychem MiniSeal page: 'Butt: M81824/1 series'); one conductor can't fill both cavities of a paired 20 A output (MoTeC PDM manual p.43/p.44 '20 A Output n (with Axx)'), so every load on OUT1-8 takes two equal pigtails and an in-line MiniSeal. Pigtail gauge makes both splice sides fit one colour (3137CT cavities 26-20 / 20-16 / 16-12): a 12-16 AWG load takes 2 x 16 AWG into M81824/1-3 (yellow); an 18-20 AWG load takes 2 x 20 AWG into M81824/1-2 (blue); a 22-24 AWG load is raised to 20 AWG first (red can't take 2 x 20). 20 AWG pigtails are inside MoTeC's 20#-16# for 20 A outputs (p.48) and carry 2 x 8 A at 80 C, so that output's limit is set to 16 A or less (review 2026-09-28, second book review))

decision: awg 22 -> 20 — a 22-24 AWG load can't share a MiniSeal colour with 2 x 20 AWG pigtails (one conductor can't fill both cavities of a paired 20 A output (MoTeC PDM manual p.43/p.44 '20 A Output n (with Axx)'), so every load on OUT1-8 takes two equal pigtails and an in-line MiniSeal. Pigtail gauge makes both splice sides fit one colour (3137CT cavities 26-20 / 20-16 / 16-12): a 12-16 AWG load takes 2 x 16 AWG into M81824/1-3 (yellow); an 18-20 AWG load takes 2 x 20 AWG into M81824/1-2 (blue); a 22-24 AWG load is raised to 20 AWG first (red can't take 2 x 20). 20 AWG pigtails are inside MoTeC's 20#-16# for 20 A outputs (p.48) and carry 2 x 8 A at 80 C, so that output's limit is set to 16 A or less (review 2026-09-28, second book review))

decision: frm PDM30:OUT5 -> SPL-PDM30-OUT5 (PDM30:OUT5 pigtails A9 + A17) — the 20 AWG load wire starts at the in-line M81824/1-2; the two 20 AWG pigtails 93_PT1/_PT2 land on PDM30 A9 and A17 (review A1 (receipt 2026-09-28_reviews-and-shape-rules.md; state 0h(1)): MoTeC PDM user manual p.48 — 20# to 16# on 20 A outputs, 16# = 15 A at 80 C, each pin carries about half the output; Superseal SSC-N contact 24-16 AWG (ProWire M800-KIT-N); in-line MiniSeal M81824/1-3 (ProWire Raychem MiniSeal page: 'Butt: M81824/1 series'); one conductor can't fill both cavities of a paired 20 A output (MoTeC PDM manual p.43/p.44 '20 A Output n (with Axx)'), so every load on OUT1-8 takes two equal pigtails and an in-line MiniSeal. wires.label: Fuel level sender -> M130 AV6 (with the Dakota #117 in parallel)
wires.notes: AV pin UNASSIGNED in cut list; 2026-05-14 Dakota addendum claimed A25/AV5 — A25 now taken by #102 (v4). Needs AV pin decision; see v4 receipt open items. | OPEN — for Dave (adjudication, not a pick): #98 (M130 AV6 with a 270 ohm pull-up to 5 V, state row 32 'Fuel sender: GM 0-90 ohm -> AV input + 270 ohm pull-up') and #117 (Dakota VHX FUEL SND) share ONE resistive sender. Physics: each instrument reads the sender by pushing its own current through it and measuring the voltage; a second source in parallel shifts that voltage, so both read wrong. Dakota VHX manual 650314:P p.11: 'The fuel sender gets power from the control box only ... make sure that the wire does not have power' — the M130 pull-up is power on that wire. p.23: the VHX reads eight resistance senders or CUSTOM, or 'BUS' (fuel level into the AUX I/O port through a BIM module); it has no 0-5 V fuel input. So the paths are: (a) the sender to the M130 only (row 32) and the VHX on BUS through a BIM-EFI-1 reading the M1 General CAN stream (state 0c fork, DAKOTA_VHX_ARCHITECTURE.md); (b) the sender to the Dakota only and no M130 fuel level; (c) a second sender in the tank. The gauge-feed lock (row 36, dual senders) kept both wires without resolving this | 270 ohm pull-up to a sensor 5 V at the ECU end (state row 32; the 5 V letter follows the A7 pairing ruling); OPEN: confirm the Dakota FUEL SND still reads true with the M130 pull-up on the same sender (bench) — DAKOTA_VHX_ARCHITECTURE.md FIX 1 flagged the pin as unassigned, not the parallel reading

wires.label: Dakota Fuel Level Sender
wires.section: DAKOTA DIGITAL VHX DUAL-SENDER (11 wires, 66.4 ft) — per 2026-05-14 addendum receipt
wires.notes: Factory GM 0-90Ω tank sender tap, parallel with #98 (ECU). Same receipt | OPEN — for Dave (adjudication, not a pick): #98 (M130 AV6 with a 270 ohm pull-up to 5 V, state row 32 'Fuel sender: GM 0-90 ohm -> AV input + 270 ohm pull-up') and #117 (Dakota VHX FUEL SND) share ONE resistive sender. Physics: each instrument reads the sender by pushing its own current through it and measuring the voltage; a second source in parallel shifts that voltage, so both read wrong. Dakota VHX manual 650314:P p.11: 'The fuel sender gets power from the control box only ... make sure that the wire does not have power' — the M130 pull-up is power on that wire. p.23: the VHX reads eight resistance senders or CUSTOM, or 'BUS' (fuel level into the AUX I/O port through a BIM module); it has no 0-5 V fuel input. So the paths are: (a) the sender to the M130 only (row 32) and the VHX on BUS through a BIM-EFI-1 reading the M1 General CAN stream (state 0c fork, DAKOTA_VHX_ARCHITECTURE.md); (b) the sender to the Dakota only and no M130 fuel level; (c) a second sender in the tank. The gauge-feed lock (row 36, dual senders) kept both wires without resolving this

implied.control: CAN: M130 fan request (MoTeC PDM manual p.39 CAN input) — OUT1 and OUT6 on one channel (p.22)

sources: fan junction (round 3 close): PDM15 OUT1 and OUT6 each feed 2 x 16 AWG pigtails into their own M81824/1-3 (2 x 2,580 = 5,160 CM, 12 AWG equivalent, in the 16-12 cavity) -> a 12 AWG leg; both legs and the 12 AWG fan tail land on FAN-JUNCTION, a Blue Sea 2103 PowerPost Plus (3/8-16 stud, 150 A) on ProWire 9918 rings (12-10 AWG, 3/8 in). The tail carries 32 A: it needs 32 / 0.85 = 37.6 A, the singles table gives 38 A — only in free air at <= 90 C ambient (the hot-soak OPEN and the outside-the-loom routing apply to the tail)

WIPER-MOTOR.device: factory 1977 C/K 2-speed wiper motor on the cowl: compound-wound 12 V DC motor, gear box with park switch, internal circuit breaker on the brush plate, terminal board 1 / 2 (center feed) / 3, ground strap; the factory washer pump rides on it
WIPER-MOTOR.note: terminal board: 2 (center) = feed; 1 = series field + armature to the dash switch (ground); 3 = shunt field to the dash switch; the 20 ohm resistor on the back of the board bridges 1 and 3 for HI; the park switch (normally closed, opened by the gear cam) holds 1 to ground after OFF so the motor parks in LO off the feed. Currents: 2.0-3.0 A and 3.5-5.0 A are the manual's bench trouble-chart readings with the wiper detached; 20+ A is the stall reading. The internal breaker protects the motor from overheating; OUT12 protects the wires. Pulse (delay) wipers used the same motor with an external control unit (p.804). Not added (the owner's plan has no delay). The PDM cannot make a delay by pulsing the center feed: park runs from that feed, so cutting it stops the blades mid-sweep. A PDM delay would need the park switch read on a PDM input to hold the feed until park; not designed. The factory washer pump on the gear box (Fig. 8-16) is left unwired: its ratchet solenoid is never energised, and the lock-out tang on the piston actuating plate keeps it from pumping (p.814 lists a broken lock-out tang as the cause of pumping all the time). The electric pump in the jar (WASHER-PUMP) replaces it.

pdm_settings.source: SPAL 30107090 'roughly 25 amp max' (web_snapshots/www.kartek.com__spal-30107090-...md); OUT1 + OUT6 through FAN-JUNCTION
pdm_settings.status: set: 16 A per output (fan junction (round 3 close): PDM15 OUT1 and OUT6 each feed 2 x 16 AWG pigtails into their own M81824/1-3 (2 x 2,580 = 5,160 CM, 12 AWG equivalent, in the 16-12 cavity) -> a 12 AWG leg; both legs and the 12 AWG fan tail land on FAN-JUNCTION, a Blue Sea 2103 PowerPost Plus (3/8-16 stud, 150 A) on ProWire 9918 rings (12-10 AWG, 3/8 in). Limits 16 A per output, 32 A total >= 1.25 x 25 A. Each output's pigtails: 2 x 12 A at 100 C (PDM manual p.48) = 24 A, 0.85 x 24 = 20.4 >= 16. Each leg carries 16 A: 12 AWG singles 38 A (ProWire singles table, 60 C difference), 0.85 x 38 = 32.3 >= 16. The tail carries 32 A: it needs 32 / 0.85 = 37.6 A, the singles table gives 38 A — only in free air at <= 90 C ambient (the hot-soak OPEN and the outside-the-loom routing apply to the tail))

PCS-CAN.name: PCS CAN out to the M130 / Dakota (gear, fluid temperature on the dash)
PCS-CAN.source:
lead 2026-09-28; research/2026-09-28_6l90-transmission-electrical.md §4: the PCS speaks J1939, GMLAN and PCS CAN, receive and transmit
      selectable (ZGP TCM-2650 setup guide rev2 p.6, p.21). Not wired: the locked ruling keeps the PCS-T43 link a private two-node bus off the
      M130 trunk (receipts/2026-07-12_6l80e-can-master-ruling.md). A third CAN link or the M130 on that bus needs an M130 J1939/GMLAN receive
      template and changes the ruling: owner decision

IBST-CAN.source:
lead 2026-09-28; research/2026-09-28_ibooster-gen2-wiring.md A4-A5: a twisted pair from the booster's vehicle CAN pins 16/25
      (Gen 1 unit 1037123-00-B: web_snapshots/www.fastandquiet.com__bosch-ibooster-gen-1-pinout.PDF.md) to a sealed diagnostic port, 120 ohm at each end,
      its own 500 kbps bus (web_snapshots/www.evcreate.com__ibooster-can-bus.md), never on the M1 trunk; read only, nothing transmitted
